This structure seems overly indirect to me, but maybe I'm misunderstanding?

My suggestion:

- `Navigation`'s activation is initially null
- `NavigationActivation`s have old entry/new entry/navigation type directly.
- "Activation info" struct does not exist
- For non initial about:blank documents, we set _document_'s relevant global object's navigation API's activation to a new `NavigationActivation`.

body:
OK, this is just further evidence I really should pass in the NavigationType to this algorithm (instead of requiring it to be re-computed).

The initial ideal was that we would just set things up nicely, and "apply the history step" would behave basically the same, with no special casing needed for each type.

However, as noted in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9826 (see especially my reply), this is not working out great. And we have the wrapper algorithms anyway, so this purity is not helping.

An important thing to note is that "apply the history step" can be called for something which is none of these four types: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-for-navigable-creation/destruction . I think this breaks your switch here.

So here's my proposal. We add a NavigationType to "apply the history step", and thread it through from all calling algorithms. (This is slightly more involved for "apply the push/replace history step".) Ideally we fix https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9826 as part of this. Then, we can just use it and not re-compute it here.

Maybe we can even add some asserts, that parallel the great work you've done here to re-derive the state from the other parameters. Or maybe we could delete the "reload pending" and "ever populated" flags!! That would be nice.
